name: Vascular Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: 2017 International Classification of the Ehlers-Danlos Syndromes

criteria.description: Family history of vEDS with documented causative COL3A1 variant
Spontaneous sigmoid colon perforation without known diverticular disease or other bowel pathology
Uterine rupture during third trimester without prior C-section or severe peri-partum perineal tears
Bruising without identified trauma and/or in unusual sites
Thin, translucent skin with visible subcutaneous vasculature
Characteristic facial appearance (thin lips, small chin, thin nose, prominent eyes)
Acrogeria (aged appearance of extremities, especially hands)
Early-onset varicose veins (before age 30 and nulliparous if female)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Any major criterion or several minor criteria should raise suspicion. Confirmatory testing requires identification of a causative COL3A1 (or rarely COL1A1) variant.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: This is the most life-threatening EDS subtype. Median life expectancy is approximately 50 years. Invasive vascular procedures carry high risk.

pathognomonic.notes: Most common cause of death; medium-sized arteries most affected

pathognomonic.symptomName: Thin translucent skin with visible veins
pathognomonic.notes: Subcutaneous venous pattern visible especially on chest and abdomen

common.notes: Thin vermilion of lips, micrognathia, thin nose, prominent eyes
Usually sigmoid colon; peak incidence in 20s-30s
Premature aging of skin on hands and feet
Generalized large-joint hypermobility is typically absent

rare.notes: Typically in third trimester; high maternal mortality risk

laboratory: Skin fibroblast culture showing abnormal type III collagen (historical method)
imaging: CT angiography for vascular surveillance (non-invasive preferred)
MR angiography as alternative to CTA
Avoid invasive catheter-based angiography due to arterial fragility
other: Skin biopsy with electron microscopy may show collagen fibril abnormalities
Non-invasive vascular assessment recommended over invasive procedures

distinguishingFeatures: cEDS has marked skin hyperextensibility (vEDS skin is thin, not hyperextensible)
cEDS has atrophic scars (vEDS bruising predominates)
cEDS confirmed by COL5A1/COL5A2, not COL3A1
LDS has aortic root aneurysm and tortuous arteries
LDS features bifid uvula or cleft palate
Marfan has tall stature and arachnodactyly
Marfan has aortic root dilation; vEDS affects medium arteries

redFlags: Sudden severe abdominal or chest pain (suspect arterial rupture or bowel perforation)
Pregnancy in confirmed vEDS (high maternal mortality risk)
Any planned invasive or surgical procedure (high complication risk)
Family history of unexplained sudden death at young age
references: Byers PH, et al. Vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome. In: GeneReviews. University of Washington, Seattle; Updated 2019.
Pepin M, et al. Clinical and genetic features of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome type IV, the vascular type. N Engl J Med. 2000;342(10):673-80.
Malfait F, et al. The 2017 International Classification of the Ehlers-Danlos Syndromes. Am J Med Genet C Semin Med Genet. 2017;175(1):8-26.
Ong KT, et al. Effect of celiprolol on prevention of cardiovascular events in vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome. Lancet. 2010;376(9751):1476-84.
